faults.title: Approval waits while the real worker process is killed; the original approval resumes the unchanged operation
faults.injection_point: OS process kill `taskkill /F /T /PID <worker-a>` of the real worker process tests/f13b/t106_worker.py (real mTLS capability + T035 waiting/exit protocol) while platform.approvals.state='pending'; restart = compiled `cmd/supervisor exec --once` process against the same PostgreSQL + mTLS API, then a fresh worker process claiming the single resume job. Durability seam: platform.approvals, platform.operations, platform.run_waitings, platform.jobs.
expected: the killed process disappears and its PostgreSQL session leaves pg_stat_activity
the approval row is not replaced (same id/proposal/params_sha256/approver)
platform.operations keeps exactly the same operation id
exactly one resume job is created, only after the human decision
the loopback endpoint observes 0 requests before approval and exactly 1 after
the resumed operation reaches succeeded with exactly one attempt

faults.title: An approval is bound to the exact params: changed params and wrong hashes are refused with zero writes
faults.injection_point: internal/capabilities/service.go:689-700 `prepareOperation` compares the stored operation's params_sha256 with the new canonical digest and returns 409 operation_conflict; internal/approvals/decision.go:148-151 compares the decision's params_sha256 with the approval and returns 409 approval_params_mismatch. exercised through the real mTLS capability and owner decision HTTP paths.
expected: a replay with changed params is refused (409 operation_conflict)
the old approval cannot authorise changed params or a different logical key
a decision with a wrong params_sha256 is refused (409 approval_params_mismatch)
a stranger (404) and the admin (403 approver_mismatch) cannot decide
a late decision after cancellation is refused (409)
every refused path leaves the loopback write count unchanged

faults.title: The connector applies the write and the connection is dropped before the receipt; the operation is unknown, never auto-resent, and reconciles to one write
faults.injection_point: tests/support/t051.py:39-70 `_DropHandler._handle` reads the complete request body (the write is really applied by the endpoint) and then calls socket.shutdown(SHUT_RDWR) with no response; the product's real HTTP client (internal/capabilities/connectors.go dispatchConnector) observes a transport error and markConnectorUnknown commits operations.state='unknown' + run_unknown_operations + runs.state='needs_reconciliation'.
expected: the endpoint observes exactly one write request
the operation is unknown (never succeeded/failed) and has no receipt
a duplicate invoke does not send a second request
the Run is not succeeded while the write is unknown (needs_reconciliation)
owner evidence + POST /operations/{id}/reconcile settles it as succeeded
the physical write count stays exactly 1
